united-states.text: Wine is made in all fifty states, and the industry rests almost entirely on European Vitis vinifera. Chardonnay and Cabernet Sauvignon are the most planted grapes at 18% each, then Pinot Noir at 10%. California makes 80.8% of all US wine.

united-states/adelaida-district.text: A Paso Robles sub-area in the Santa Lucia Range, with mountain slopes and foothills from 900 to 2,200 feet around the small town of Adelaida.

united-states/alexander-valley.text: A valley appellation in northeastern Sonoma County, just north of Healdsburg, within the North Coast and Northern Sonoma. The Pine Mountain-Cloverdale Peak AVA sits inside it.

united-states/alisos-canyon.text: A small Central Coast AVA in Santa Barbara County east of Los Alamos on US 101, about 20 miles south of Santa Maria.

united-states/alta-mesa.text: A Lodi sub-area in Sacramento County, about 21 miles south of downtown Sacramento. It is one of seven smaller areas drawn within Lodi, which stays a single AVA.

united-states/ancient-lakes-of-columbia-.text: A Columbia Valley sub-area in central Washington near Quincy, on the western edge of the Columbia Basin in the Quincy Basin.

united-states/anderson-valley.text: A western Mendocino County valley along the Navarro River, known mainly for Pinot Noir and sparkling wine. As of 2025 about 2,457 acres are planted across roughly 100 vineyards in a 57,600 acre area within Mendocino and North Coast.

united-states/antelope-valley-of-the-cal.text: A high desert California AVA across southern Kern County and northeastern Los Angeles County, circling the cities of Lancaster and Palmdale. It covers 426,000 acres.

wiki.title: Antelope Valley of the California High Desert AVA

united-states/applegate-valley.text: A valley along the Applegate River in Southern Oregon, in Jackson and Josephine Counties near Jacksonville.

united-states/arroyo-grande-valley.text: A 16 mile Central Coast valley in San Luis Obispo County where Pacific breezes moderate the climate and a fog line divides it. Zinfandel, Petite Sirah and Rhone varieties are grown on the higher elevations near Lopez Lake.

united-states/arroyo-seco.text: A triangular Monterey County AVA beside Arroyo Seco Creek in the Salinas Valley, near Soledad. Its closeness to the Pacific gives a maritime climate suited to cool climate grapes.

united-states/atlas-peak.text: A Napa Valley sub-area on the western slope of the Vaca Range, northeast of the city of Napa, around a peak of 2,663 feet.

united-states/ballard-canyon.text: A 7,800 acre canyon in the center of the Santa Ynez Valley in Santa Barbara County, between Los Olivos, Ballard and Solvang.

united-states/ben-lomond-mountain.text: An AVA on the coastal edge of the Santa Cruz Mountains in Santa Cruz County, covering about 38,400 acres.

united-states/benmore-valley.text: A high, cool North Coast depression in the mountains of southwestern Lake County, at 2,400 feet and much cooler than surrounding areas. At the outset about 125 acres grew Chardonnay. It is named for Ben Moore, a 19th century cattle rustler.

united-states/bennett-valley.text: Sonoma Valley's smallest AVA at 8,140 acres, ringed by the Sonoma Mountains southeast of Santa Rosa. It lies within the North Coast and overlaps Sonoma Valley, Sonoma Coast and Sonoma Mountain.

united-states/big-valley-district-lake-c.text: A Clear Lake sub-area on the western shore of the lake, covering the flatter half of the valley north of Kelseyville. Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay, Viognier and Riesling are the main whites, while Zinfandel, Merlot and Cabernet Franc lead the reds.

united-states/borden-ranch.text: A Lodi sub-area in southern Sacramento and northern San Joaquin Counties, about 27 miles southeast of Sacramento, taking in the community of Clay. It is one of seven smaller areas within Lodi, which stays a single AVA.

united-states/california.text: A US wine state with roots in the Spanish missions of the late 1700s. After Prohibition it was known mostly for sweet, port-style and jug wines, then gained international standing at the Paris Wine Tasting of 1976. Its areas include Napa Valley, Sonoma County, the Central Coast and Lodi.

united-states/california-shenandoah-vall.text: A Sierra Foothills AVA across parts of Amador and El Dorado Counties, north and west of Fiddletown, with about 1,200 of its 10,000 acres under vine.

united-states/calistoga.text: A Napa Valley sub-area in the northwest of the county, around but not covering the whole town of Calistoga. The name dates to 1857, with first vines planted in 1862.

united-states/candy-mountain.text: A small Columbia Valley AVA on the slopes of Candy Mountain in Benton County, southwest of Richland along the Columbia River, inside Yakima Valley. Wines need at least 85% local grapes.

united-states/capay-valley.text: A California valley AVA in northwestern Yolo County, in plant hardiness zones 9a and 9b. At the outset only about 25 acres were planted.

united-states/carmel-valley.text: A Central Coast AVA in Monterey County, about 5 miles inland within the Santa Lucia Range, southeast of Carmel-by-the-Sea. About 300 acres of grapes grow at elevations from 203 to 2,762 feet, and some vineyards date to the 1870s.

united-states/cayuga-lake.text: A Finger Lakes sub-area in upstate New York across Cayuga, Seneca and Tompkins counties. Most vineyards sit in shale soils on hillsides along the lake's western side, where the lake and steep slopes extend the growing season.

united-states/central-coast.text: A large AVA along California's Pacific coast from the San Francisco Bay Area south through Monterey, San Luis Obispo and Santa Barbara Counties, with a shared maritime climate. It holds dozens of AVAs, including Paso Robles, Edna Valley and Santa Maria Valley.

united-states/chalk-hill.text: A Sonoma County AVA about eight miles north of Santa Rosa, in the northeast corner of Russian River Valley. Its name comes from a hill with chalky white volcanic tuff in the soil, ash from the volcanic activity of Mount Saint Helena.

united-states/chalone.text: A Gabilan Mountains AVA on the Monterey and San Benito County line, east of Soledad, inside the Central Coast.

united-states/champlain-valley-of-new-yo.text: A New York AVA in the northeastern corner, beside the Canadian and Vermont borders. Its short growing season suits cold-hardy hybrids such as Frontenac, La Crescent and Marquette, not the vinifera grapes grown in surrounding areas.

wiki.title: Champlain Valley of New York AVA

united-states/chehalem-mountains.text: A Willamette Valley AVA on a single uplifted landmass of ridges over 20 miles long, about 19 miles southwest of Portland, with Laurelwood District and Ribbon Ridge inside it.

united-states/chiles-valley.text: A Napa Valley sub-area in the Vaca Mountains on the northeast side, level with St. Helena and Rutherford.

united-states/cienega-valley.text: A San Benito County AVA at about 1,100 feet, split by the San Andreas Fault: granite and sandstone soils on the east side, granite and limestone on the west. It grows some of the oldest Pinot Noir vines in California.

united-states/clarksburg.text: A California AVA in the Sacramento Valley across Sacramento, Solano and Yolo Counties, with dense clay, silt and loam soils, kept cooler than Sacramento by fog and breezes from San Francisco Bay. Ninety percent of its grapes go to wineries elsewhere, so few wines carry its name.

united-states/clear-lake.text: A North Coast AVA in Lake County, centered on Clear Lake, the largest natural fresh water lake within California. Sub-areas include Big Valley District, High Valley, Kelsey Bench and Red Hills.

united-states/clements-hills.text: A Lodi sub-area in northern San Joaquin County around the town of Clements, about 41 miles southeast of Sacramento. It is one of seven smaller areas within Lodi.

united-states/cole-ranch.text: A tiny Mendocino County AVA on a 500 acre ranch in a narrow mountain valley between Boonville and Highway 101. The valley is about a mile long and half a mile across, among hills 1,400 to 1,600 feet high.

united-states/columbia-gorge.text: An AVA along the Columbia River Gorge on the Washington and Oregon border, marketed as a world of wine in 40 miles for its wide range of climate and terroir. Pinot Noir leads plantings at 24%, then Chardonnay at 20%.

united-states/columbia-valley.text: A huge AVA covering much of central and southern Washington and crossing into northern Oregon, across the Columbia River Plateau. It contains Walla Walla Valley, Yakima Valley, Red Mountain and Horse Heaven Hills.

united-states/comptche.text: A Mendocino County AVA kept separate from the North Coast AVA because of its own topography, soils and climate. Its boundaries follow the 400 foot contour, which divides the valley floor from higher, forested land.

united-states/contra-costa.text: A California AVA in the San Francisco Bay Area, east of San Pablo Bay, around Concord, Martinez, Antioch and Brentwood. It has at least 14 wineries and about 1,700 acres of vines, with Zinfandel the most commonly grown grape.

united-states/coombsville.text: A Napa Valley sub-area just east of the city of Napa, where cool marine air and fog from San Pablo Bay arrive almost daily. Soils are volcanic, with rhyolitic tuff and lava from the Vaca Range.

united-states/cosumnes-river.text: A Lodi sub-area in northwestern Sacramento County along the lower Cosumnes River, bordering the town of Galt, about 20 miles south of Sacramento. It is one of seven smaller areas within Lodi, which stays a single AVA.

united-states/covelo.text: A northern Mendocino County AVA about 150 miles north of San Francisco, covering Round and Williams Valleys. It spans 38,000 acres yet had only 2 acres under vine at the outset.

united-states/creston-district.text: A Paso Robles sub-area in the southeast, covering 47,000 acres with 1,365 acres of vineyards. It lies on an old erosional plateau at the base of the La Panza Range, with alluvial terraces and fans.

united-states/crystal-springs-of-napa-va.text: A small California AVA created in 2024 inside Napa Valley, overlapping none of its neighbors. Its borders were drawn to take in the Crystal Springs Vineyard, part of which had been in Calistoga.

wiki.title: Crystal Springs of Napa Valley AVA

united-states/cucamonga-valley.text: A warm California AVA across Riverside and San Bernardino Counties, about 15 miles west of San Bernardino, where summer highs often pass 100°F. The valley floor has sandy, alluvial soils. Wines need at least 85% local grapes to carry the name.

united-states/diablo-grande.text: A California AVA in the western foothills of Stanislaus County, all on private land within a gated resort community. Its 30,000 acres have vineyards at 1,000 to 1,800 feet.

united-states/diamond-mountain-district.text: A Napa Valley sub-area in the northwest, higher than most of the valley, so it gets less cool fog and more direct sun. Its very porous soil cools quickly. The southern part of Calistoga town lies inside it.

united-states/dos-rios.text: A northern Mendocino County AVA in canyons holding two rivers, where marine breezes keep summers cooler and winters warmer than inland areas to the east. As of 2023 only six acres of commercial vineyard are planted.

united-states/dry-creek-valley.text: A north-central Sonoma County valley northwest of Healdsburg, 20 miles from the Pacific. It is shaped like an inverted U, about 16 miles long and two wide.

united-states/dundee-hills.text: A Willamette Valley AVA in Yamhill County near Newberg, with reddish Jory silt, clay and loam soils. The Chehalem Mountains shelter it from cool Columbia Gorge winds. David Lett established Eyrie Vineyards there in 1966, and the valley grows mostly Pinot Noir.

united-states/dunnigan-hills.text: A California AVA of low, rolling hills in Yolo County, covering 89,000 acres, with a Mediterranean climate less prone to frost than other Sacramento Valley areas.

united-states/eagle-peak-mendocino-count.text: A mountainous AVA in northern Mendocino County, in the Coastal Range west of Redwood Valley, about ten miles north of Ukiah. It lies within the North Coast. The county grows mostly Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Cabernet Sauvignon.

united-states/edna-valley.text: A Central Coast valley in San Luis Obispo County with cool maritime fog, moderate sunshine, and volcanic, clay-rich soils with black humus. Those conditions give it California's longest growing season. It lies nine miles southeast of San Luis Obispo.

united-states/el-dorado.text: A Sierra Foothills AVA centered on Placerville in El Dorado County, east of Sacramento. At 1.09 million acres it takes in all of Fair Play and part of California Shenandoah Valley. The county grows mostly Zinfandel at 22%, then Cabernet Sauvignon.

united-states/el-pomar-district.text: A Paso Robles sub-area in the central part, southeast of the city of Paso Robles, covering 21,300 acres.

united-states/elkton-oregon.text: A Douglas County AVA around the town of Elkton, inside the Umpqua Valley.

united-states/eola-amity-hills.text: A Willamette Valley AVA of hills west of the Willamette River, from Amity south to Salem, in Polk and Yamhill Counties. Summers are cooler and wetter than in Washington or California.

united-states/fair-play.text: A Sierra Foothills AVA in El Dorado County, with rolling hills at 2,000 to 3,000 feet on decomposed granite soils. Zinfandel is the most popular red, alongside Rhone and Italian varieties such as Syrah, Grenache and Sangiovese.

united-states/fiddletown.text: An Amador County AVA in the Sierra Foothills, with vineyards mostly in the south and west on slopes at 1,500 to 2,500 feet. About 310 acres are planted, and the county grows mostly Zinfandel at 59%.

united-states/finger-lakes.text: Upstate New York's largest wine region, spanning 14 counties about 25 miles south of Lake Ontario. Cayuga and Seneca Lakes are sub-areas defined by lake effect. In Yates, Seneca and Ontario Counties, Catawba and Riesling are the most planted grapes.

united-states/fort-ross-seaview.text: A coastal AVA in Sonoma County between Jenner and Sea Ranch, defined by its higher elevation. It lies entirely within Sonoma Coast and the North Coast, and covers 27,000 acres about 65 miles north-northwest of San Francisco.

united-states/fountaingrove-district.text: A Sonoma County AVA northeast of Santa Rosa around the historic community of Fountain Grove, covering 38,000 acres with about 500 under vine. Grown grapes include Cabernet Sauvignon, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Zinfandel, Syrah and Viognier.

united-states/gabilan-mountains.text: A California mountain AVA on the Monterey and San Benito County line that includes Chalone and Mt. Harlan. At an average 2,370 feet it sits above the fog, so the air is cool without the humidity, and it has 4 wineries and 6 vineyards.

united-states/goose-gap.text: A Benton County AVA around Goose Mountain between Kiona and Richland, within Yakima Valley and Columbia Valley. It is named for a common path of migratory waterfowl. Main grapes are Cabernet Sauvignon, Chardonnay, Merlot and Syrah.

united-states/grand-river-valley.text: An AVA in northeastern Ohio, 45 miles east of Cleveland, across Ashtabula, Lake and Geauga Counties. It lies entirely within the larger multi-state Lake Erie AVA, which was established on the same date.

united-states/green-valley-of-russian-ri.text: A Sonoma County AVA within Russian River Valley, formerly called Sonoma County Green Valley. It covers about 36,467 acres west of the Santa Rosa Plain, in the southwestern corner of Russian River Valley.

wiki.title: Green Valley of Russian River Valley AVA

united-states/guenoc-valley.text: A small inland North Coast valley AVA in southern Lake County, on an alluvial fan, isolated from surrounding areas by rocky ridges. It gets slightly less rain than nearby Middletown.

united-states/hames-valley.text: A small east to west valley in southern Monterey County, near the San Luis Obispo County line, west of the Salinas River.

united-states/happy-canyon-of-santa-barb.text: A Santa Ynez Valley sub-area in Santa Barbara County, made of canyon, hills and creek basins east of the San Rafael Mountains, with elevations from 500 to 3,430 feet.

wiki.title: Happy Canyon of Santa Barbara AVA

united-states/high-valley.text: A Lake County AVA east of Clear Lake at 1,600 to 3,000 feet, with a valley floor and hillsides. Its east to west orientation, unusual for the Coast Range, comes from volcanic activity of Round Mountain, a dormant cinder cone.

united-states/horse-heaven-hills.text: A south-central Washington AVA within Columbia Valley, south of Yakima Valley and north of the Columbia River, with about 6,400 acres of vines. Cabernet Sauvignon covers 43% of plantings, then Merlot at 16% and Chardonnay at 12%.

united-states/howell-mountain.text: A Napa Valley AVA in Napa County, the second sub-appellation within it, set in the Vaca Range around the town of Angwin. Its boundary is set by vineyards at or above 1,400 feet.

united-states/hudson-river-region.text: A New York AVA around the Hudson River in the southeast, covering about 2.2 million acres across Columbia, Dutchess, Putnam and parts of other counties. In Ulster County, Seyval Blanc and De Chaunac are the leading grapes.

united-states/inwood-valley.text: A small California AVA in southern Shasta County, about 22 miles from Redding along State Route 44 toward Lassen Volcanic National Park.

united-states/isle-st-george.text: An AVA on North Bass Island, an island in Lake Erie in Ohio, inside the Lake Erie AVA. The island is owned by Meier's Wine Cellars, and historically over half of it was used to grow grapevines.

united-states/jahant.text: A Lodi sub-area in the center of Lodi, mostly in San Joaquin County, 29 miles south of Sacramento. It is one of seven smaller areas within Lodi.

united-states/kelsey-bench-lake-county.text: A Lake County AVA on the western side of Clear Lake, about 9,100 acres south of Big Valley District, with which it shares a valley. Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay, Viognier and Riesling are the principal whites.

united-states/knights-valley.text: A Sonoma County AVA in the Knights Valley landform, 5.3 miles long and 1.8 wide, within the North Coast and Northern Sonoma.

united-states/lake-chelan.text: A Columbia Valley sub-area in Chelan County, north-central Washington, with 24,040 acres in the southern and eastern Lake Chelan Valley and Cascade foothills. Syrah leads plantings at 33%, then Chardonnay at 17% and Pinot Gris at 14%.

united-states/lake-erie.text: A multi-state AVA along Lake Erie's southern shore across New York, Pennsylvania and Ohio, covering 2.24 million acres. It includes the Chautauqua-Erie Grape Belt, a sixty mile stretch of shoreline, and holds Grand River Valley and Isle St. George.

united-states/lamorinda.text: A San Francisco Bay Area AVA east of the Berkeley Hills in Contra Costa County, named by blending Lafayette, Moraga and Orinda. It covers about 30,000 acres, within the San Francisco Bay and Central Coast AVAs.

united-states/laurelwood-district.text: A Willamette Valley AVA at the northern end, inside Chehalem Mountains and west of Portland, covering about 33,600 acres. The Chehalem Mountains and a unique soil profile define it.

united-states/leona-valley.text: A long, narrow California valley in northeastern Los Angeles County, in the Sierra Pelona Mountains, about 50 miles inland. Portal Ridge divides it from Antelope Valley.

united-states/lime-kiln-valley.text: A small 2,300 acre AVA at the southern end of Cienega Valley in San Benito County. Summer days run 85 to 95°F with up to 50°F swings, on sandy, gravelly loam over limestone and dolomite. Old vine Mourvedre and Zinfandel grow here.

united-states/livermore-valley.text: An Alameda County AVA centered on the city of Livermore in the Tri-Valley, inside the San Francisco Bay and Central Coast AVAs. Robert Livermore, a 19th century landowner, planted its first grapevines.

united-states/lodi.text: A California Central Valley AVA at the northern edge of the San Joaquin Valley, in Sacramento and San Joaquin Counties. A 2002 expansion added 159,500 acres, with 10,840 under vine. Its seven sub-areas include Alta Mesa, Borden Ranch and Mokelumne River.

united-states/long-island.text: A New York AVA covering Nassau and Suffolk counties, including offshore islands, with the North Fork and the Hamptons inside. In Suffolk County, Merlot leads plantings at 32%, then Chardonnay at 22% and Cabernet Franc at 11%.

united-states/long-valley-lake-county.text: A California AVA in Lake County, on elevated land east of Clear Lake, in plant hardiness zones 8b to 9b. At the outset it had 3 wineries and 5 vineyards on about 149 acres.

united-states/los-carneros.text: An AVA across southern Sonoma and Napa counties just north of San Pablo Bay, also called Carneros. Fog and breezes from the bay make it cooler than regions farther north in both valleys, suiting cool climate varieties.

united-states/los-olivos-district.text: A Santa Ynez Valley AVA in Santa Barbara County, across the valley between the Purisima Hills and Solvang, taking in Los Olivos, Ballard, Santa Ynez and Solvang.

united-states/lower-long-tom.text: A southern Willamette Valley AVA near Junction City and Monroe, about 20 miles northwest of Eugene, west of the Long Tom River. It is primarily known for Pinot Noir and Pinot Gris.

united-states/madera.text: A San Joaquin Valley AVA across Madera and part of Fresno counties, with 31,179 acres of wine grapes. It produces 10% of all wine grapes grown in California.

united-states/malibu-coast.text: A long, narrow California AVA along the Pacific coast in the Santa Monica Mountains, across Los Angeles and Ventura Counties, covering about 44,590 acres. Saddle Rock-Malibu and Malibu-Newton Canyon sit inside.

united-states/malibu-newton-canyon.text: A Malibu Coast sub-area lying entirely within Newton Canyon, a bowl-shaped mountain basin below Castro Peak in the Santa Monica Mountains. Its only vineyards are on the 250 acre Rosenthal estate.

united-states/manton-valley.text: A stream-cut California valley AVA across Shasta and Tehama Counties, with a flat to gently rolling floor at 2,000 to 3,500 feet. Topography, climate and soils set it apart.

united-states/mcdowell-valley.text: A small Mendocino County AVA near Hopland, slightly cooler than the areas around it. One winery, McDowell Valley Vineyards, works there, with an emphasis on Syrah. It sits inside Mendocino and the North Coast.

united-states/mcminnville.text: A Willamette Valley AVA in Yamhill County, defined only by elevation between 200 and 1,000 feet, where shallow, infertile, uplifted marine sedimentary loams and silt differ from surrounding soils.

united-states/mendocino.text: A 283,300 acre AVA in Mendocino County, within the North Coast, spanning eight valleys including Anderson Valley, Potter Valley and Redwood Valley, with about 13 percent suitable for grapes. Sub-areas include Mendocino Ridge, Cole Ranch and McDowell Valley.

united-states/mendocino-county.text: A county appellation for wine from grapes grown mostly in Mendocino County, one of California's largest and most climatically diverse regions, with two climate zones split by the Mendocino Range. Nearly 25% of plantings are organic, and Chardonnay leads at 27%.

united-states/mendocino-ridge.text: A coastal, cool climate, high altitude AVA of ridges at or above 1,200 feet beside the Pacific in Mendocino County. Its western edge follows about 36 miles of the southern Mendocino coast, with the Navarro River to the north.

united-states/merritt-island.text: A Clarksburg sub-area on an island in the Sacramento River Delta, in Yolo County, six miles south of Sacramento. It is about 6 miles long and 1.6 wide, with cool breezes and fog from San Francisco Bay and fertile loam soil.
